rationales: Alkali metals have an outer configuration of ns¹, not ns².
This is the characteristic valence-shell configuration of alkali metals.
ns²np⁵ is characteristic of halogens, not alkali metals.
ns¹np is not the characteristic outer configuration of alkali metals.
Chalk solution is a suspension rather than the usual textbook example of a colloid showing the Tyndall effect.
Paints are colloids and show the Tyndall effect.
Sugar solution is a true solution and does not show the Tyndall effect.
Jelly is a colloid and shows the Tyndall effect, so this and paints make the item ambiguous.
External pressure affects a liquid's boiling point.
Intermolecular forces affect a liquid's boiling point.
The initial temperature affects how soon the liquid boils, not its boiling point.
The nature of the liquid affects its boiling point.
NaCl is soluble in water.
Benzene (C₆H₆) is nonpolar and is not soluble in water.
MgCl₂ is soluble in water.
KBr is soluble in water.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
N₂ has a complete octet around each nitrogen atom.
O₂ has a complete octet around each oxygen atom.
NH₃ has a complete octet around nitrogen.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among these halogens.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is about 4.0, not 1.0.
2.6 is not the accepted value for fluorine.
The Pauling electronegativity of fluorine is approximately 4.0.
3.0 is lower than fluorine's accepted value.
The K shell has one subshell.
The M shell has three subshells: 3s, 3p, and 3d.
The O shell has five subshells.
The L shell has two subshells.
One water molecule has a mass of approximately 18 atomic mass units.
18 g is the mass of one mole of water, not one molecule.
18 mg is not the mass of one water molecule.
18 kg is not the mass of one water molecule.
A triple covalent bond contains six shared electrons, not eight.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons make two shared pairs, as in a double bond.
Three is the number of shared pairs, not the number of electrons.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass of these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is the heaviest option and diffuses most slowly.
J.J. Thomson proposed the plum-pudding model, not the concept of atomic orbits.
Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom.
Bohr introduced defined orbits for electrons around the nucleus.
Planck developed the quantum theory, not the concept of atomic orbits.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Butter is a gel-type colloid, with liquid dispersed in a solid-like medium.
Bronze is a solid solution of solids, not a liquid-in-solid colloid.
Fog is a liquid dispersed in a gas.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table.
Rows is another name for horizontal periods, not vertical columns.
Blocks classify elements by the subshell being filled and are not the vertical columns.
The second and third periods are called short periods.
Normal periods usually refers to the fourth and fifth periods.
The second and third periods are not long periods.
Very long periods refers to the sixth and seventh periods.
